solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Where leaves are stored ready for burning? (9,5)

annotation.definition: Where leaves are stored ready for burning?

blocks.note: the surface wants a garden heap or a book's pages; the setter means shredded tobacco leaf wrapped up
not a bonfire but a smoke, rolled and waiting to be lit

annotation.surface: Someone asks where the autumn leaves are kept until the bonfire.
annotation.walkthrough: Leaves suggest a garden heap or the pages of a book; the burning points instead to a smoker rolling tobacco leaf in a thin paper.
annotation.definitionFit: A cigarette paper holds shredded tobacco leaf until the cigarette is lit.

entries.clue: Bend to hear the Speaker and part of Conservative policy (7)

blocks.note: to be in something is to be part of it
C = Conservative
a party line is its policy

annotation.surface: An MP leans forward in the Commons to catch the Speaker and toe the Tory line.
annotation.walkthrough: The Speaker chairs the House of Commons, so the surface stays in Parliament; the definition is simply leaning your head towards someone talking.
annotation.definitionFit: To incline is to bend or lean, as you do towards a speaker you are straining to hear.

entries.clue: Country in state, having installed a Labour leader (9)

indicatorNotes.having installed: the state has the new letters put inside it

blocks.note: Austria is a state; it opens up after AUSTR
A plus L, the first letter of Labour, installed inside

annotation.surface: A country's politics: a state that has just installed a Labour leader.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an election result; Austria is the state, and one of its own neighbours in the grid of nations comes out once A and L go in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by category: the answer is a nation, and the clue's state is a different one, Austria.

entries.clue: Ultimately becomes excited by butts (4,2)

indicatorNotes.by: by = beside: UP sits next to ENDS

blocks.note: cigarette butts are the ends
worked up = excited

annotation.surface: Someone gets steadily more worked up by cigarette butts, or by bottoms.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards from the clue: 'excited' comes first but UP goes last, placed by ENDS.
annotation.definitionFit: Whatever someone ends up as is what they ultimately become.

entries.clue: Philosophy piece with weak introductory part (8)

blocks.note: thin = weak, and it forms the opening
a chess piece

annotation.surface: A critic dismisses a philosophy essay whose opening section is feeble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' sounds like an essay; it is a chess piece, with the weak part tacked on in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone's thinking is their philosophy, their way of seeing things.

entries.clue: Stuffy male brought out with soldiers preceding (5)

indicatorNotes.brought out: the male's letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: PRIM (stuffy) with M for male removed
OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers

annotation.surface: A pompous man is escorted from the room with troops leading the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preceding' looks like it places the soldiers in front, but it is the definition, and OR goes last.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prior engagement is one that comes earlier, as in 'the preceding week'.

entries.clue: Post Office counter and safe to be put away (7)

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
a counter is a table you serve across

annotation.surface: At the post office counter, the safe is locked up for the night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' is slang for drinking, not storing, and 'safe' is an adjective, not a strongbox.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means drinkable, and 'put away' is informal English for drinking or eating something down.

entries.clue: What might be needed for torn Nice courts? (14)

annotation.definition: What might be needed for torn Nice courts?

indicatorNotes.What might be needed for: the fodder needs rebuilding, that is, rearranging

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters
anagram indicator: torn things need rebuilding, so the letters get rearranged

annotation.surface: Tennis courts in Nice have been ripped up and need rebuilding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Torn' is both the indicator and part of the fodder: all of TORN NICE COURTS gets rearranged, which is exactly what rebuilding them would be.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: ripped-up tennis courts need rebuilding, and rebuilding the letters is exactly the anagram.

entries.clue: Dish of beaten frogs awful, female admitted (4,10)

indicatorNotes.awful: awful signals the letters are in a mess
indicatorNotes.admitted: the F is let in among the other letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters
F = female, admitted to the fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A grim menu item: whipped frogs, with a woman let into the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' belongs to the fodder, not the joining words; frogs' legs make French cookery the obvious guess, but the dish is Russian.
annotation.definitionFit: Beef stroganoff is a dish of beef strips in a sour-cream sauce.

entries.clue: Formerly damned without right and pardoned (7)

indicatorNotes.without: without = lacking: the R is dropped

blocks.note: ex = former
CURSED (damned) minus R for right

annotation.surface: Someone once condemned, and without justice, has since been pardoned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' is a letter to lose, not a moral point; the definition sits at the end after 'and'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pupil let off a punishment has been forgiven, or pardoned.

entries.clue: I do it mixed with dash of icing (cold and half-baked) (7)

indicatorNotes.mixed: the letters of I DO IT are stirred together
indicatorNotes.dash of: a dash is just a little: the first letter

blocks.note: anagram of I DO IT
first letter of icing
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A baker explains a recipe: mix it with a little icing, keep it cold, bake it partly.
annotation.walkthrough: The cake words make 'half-baked' look like a cooking instruction; it is the definition, meaning foolish.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a half-baked scheme is one not properly thought through, which is to say foolish.

entries.clue: Hood’s crony chippy perhaps eavesdropped on getting food (5,4)

indicatorNotes.eavesdropped on: what is overheard is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a chippy (fish-and-chip shop) is an example of a fryer
tuck is British school slang for food

annotation.surface: A gangster's pal listens in at the fish-and-chip shop while picking up dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hood' suggests a gangster; it is Robin Hood, whose band included the portly Friar Tuck. A chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop.
annotation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is one of Robin Hood's Merry Men.

entries.clue: Singer appearing embarrassed about their chest? (5)

annotation.definition: Singer appearing embarrassed about their chest?

blocks.note: the surface wants a vocalist; the setter means a songbird
red in the face becomes red on the breast, the bird's famous marking

annotation.surface: A self-conscious vocalist blushes over their figure.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer is a bird, and the red face of embarrassment is really a robin's red breast.
annotation.definitionFit: The robin is a songbird famous for its red breast.

entries.clue: Shake a little, wanting medium-sized drink (6)

blocks.note: to tremble is to shake slightly
M = medium, as on clothing labels; it is the letter taken out

annotation.surface: A bartender is told to shake the cocktail lightly, skipping the medium-sized one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medium-sized drink' reads as one phrase; the break falls after 'medium-sized', which is just M, as on clothing labels.
annotation.definitionFit: A treble is a triple measure of spirits.

entries.clue: Very needy princess involved with Guy Chambers (8)

indicatorNotes.Chambers: to chamber is to enclose: GENT holds nothing here, but the clue treats IN DI as housed with GENT

blocks.note: a standing sense: someone in on a plan, or in a project, is involved in it
Princess Diana
guy = man = gent

annotation.surface: A struggling royal gets involved with the songwriter Guy Chambers.
annotation.walkthrough: Guy Chambers is a real pop songwriter, which welds the two words together; split them, and Guy is GENT.
annotation.definitionFit: Indigent means very poor, in real need.

entries.clue: Seriously hot and dread taking top off near home (2,7)

indicatorNotes.taking top off: the first letter comes away (in a down clue the top is the start)
indicatorNotes.near: near means close beside, so the ear piece is placed right up against the home

blocks.note: hot = fashionable = in
FEAR without its first letter
a nest is a bird's home

annotation.surface: Someone is truly sweating with dread as they get close to home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot' means fashionable here, not temperature.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: meaning what you say, not joking, is the adverb's sense.

entries.clue: Fruity sort holding close upper-class swinger (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: PLUM holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a plum is a sort of fruit; it opens after P
the close is the end
U = upper-class

annotation.surface: A saucy posh type keeps a swinging partner close.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a partygoer; it is anything that swings, like a clock's pendulum.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the weight in a clock case that goes to and fro is literally something that swings.

entries.clue: Old fruits hanging around about dragonflies? (8)

indicatorNotes.hanging around: DATES hang around the letters ON

blocks.note: O = old
dates go around ON: D + ON + ATES
on = about, as in a talk on a topic

annotation.surface: Stale fruit is left out and dragonflies come buzzing around it.
annotation.walkthrough: Odonata is the insect order of dragonflies and damselflies; the question mark flags that any one member is an odonate.
annotation.definitionFit: Odonates are insects of the order Odonata, the dragonflies and damselflies.

entries.clue: One tragically set up new hotel on foundationless lot (7)

indicatorNotes.new: new = remade: the letters of HOTEL are rearranged
indicatorNotes.foundationless: in a down clue the foundation is the last letter, which goes

blocks.note: anagram of HOTEL
LOT without its bottom letter

annotation.surface: A developer's plan: build a new hotel on a plot with no foundations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set up' looks like building the hotel; it belongs to the definition, since Othello is framed by Iago in Shakespeare's tragedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Othello is the tragic hero whom Iago sets up to believe his wife unfaithful.

entries.clue: Copper is on the walkie-talkie for so long (3,3)

indicatorNotes.on the walkie-talkie: a radio carries what is said, so the sound counts

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, read out as two letters

annotation.surface: A police officer on the radio signs off for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman, which suits the walkie-talkie; it is the metal, symbol Cu.
annotation.definitionFit: So long and see you are both casual ways to say goodbye.

entries.clue: Police and their power to get part for an old ship? (7)

blocks.note: Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police
the long arm of the law

annotation.surface: The police use their authority to seize a piece of an old ship.
annotation.walkthrough: A yardarm is either end of the spar that holds a square sail on a sailing ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: each outer end of the spar carrying a square sail is one component of a sailing ship's rigging.

entries.clue: Type seen tailing a small group (6)

indicatorNotes.tailing: tailing = following behind: SORT comes after A S

blocks.note: the article as printed
S = small, as on clothing labels
a type is a sort

annotation.surface: A certain kind of person is spotted following a little gang.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Group' looks like a noun but is a verb, the definition; to assort is to sort into groups.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sort things into classes is to group them.

entries.clue: This girl’s after top tip for air and fire signs (5)

indicatorNotes.after: after means coming later, so the girl's letters follow the tip rather than lead
indicatorNotes.top tip for: the top tip is the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of air
this girl is = she is = SHE'S

annotation.surface: An astrologer notes that a girl favours air and fire signs.
annotation.walkthrough: Air and fire are elements of the zodiac, which is the trap; the signs of a fire are its ashes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the grey residue left in the grate is the evidence, or sign, of a fire.

entries.clue: Way in which author gets wasted (5)

indicatorNotes.in which: the author goes inside the way

blocks.note: ST = street, a way; it opens around the pen
a pen writes, as an author does

annotation.surface: A writer loses themself down a road, drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' reads as drunk; the definition means used up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: energy or money used up and gone has been wasted.

entries.clue: Soldier and sailor about to go on leave (6,3)

indicatorNotes.to go on: the reversed sailor is added on after DESERT

blocks.note: to desert is to leave
a tar is a sailor, turned about

annotation.surface: An army man and a seaman are about to go on leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On leave' looks like holiday; 'leave' is a verb giving DESERT, and the Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a soldier of the 7th Armoured Division in the Second World War.

entries.clue: One might gush over turning 51 in a positive way (3,4)

blocks.note: O = over, from cricket scorecards
LI is 51 in Roman numerals, turning to IL
well = in a good way

annotation.surface: A gushing person raves over reaching 51 and taking it positively.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gush' suggests effusive praise, which the birthday picture supports; it is crude oil spurting from a well.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a newly struck crude well can spout a gusher into the air.

entries.clue: Old horse brought back by mineral plant (7)

indicatorNotes.brought back: the old horse is written backwards
indicatorNotes.by: by = beside: GANO sits next to ORE

blocks.note: ore is mined mineral
O = old
a nag is a horse; O NAG brought back reads GANO

annotation.surface: An aged horse is led back to the mine's processing plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mineral plant' looks like an industrial works; the plant is the herb.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is a Mediterranean herb of the mint family, used in pizza and Greek cooking.

entries.clue: Where Doctor Who travels occasionally (4,4,2,4)

blocks.note: the Doctor journeys from one time to another in the TARDIS
now and then

annotation.surface: Doctor Who only travels now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC show about a time traveller.
annotation.definitionFit: From time to time means occasionally, and it is literally the Doctor's itinerary.
